solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lay cryptic clues before adult readers primarily

indicators.note: something cryptic is obscure and disguised, so the word clues is scrambled out of recognition

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: primarily points to what comes first, so only the opening letter of readers is used

parts.note: the initial letter of readers

explanation.surface: Someone sets out puzzling clues ahead of grown-up readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' places the rearranged CLUES ahead of A and R, giving SECULAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay as an adjective means not belonging to the clergy, which is the core sense of secular, worldly rather than religious.

clue.text: Special pointer finds bird

parts.note: sp is a standard abbreviation of special
an arrow is a sign that points the way

explanation.surface: A specially trained gun dog locates a game bird.
explanation.walkthrough: A pointer is a gun dog, which fits the bird in the surface, but here it is an arrow.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparrow is a small brown songbird, common in towns and gardens.

clue.text: Egalitarian girl is into non-U clues by us

indicators.note: by means beside, so the two shortened words sit next to each other
is into means goes inside, so the girl sits within the remaining letters
non-U literally says no U, so every U is removed from the words that follow

parts.note: taken as written, then losing its U
a lass is a girl
taken as written, then losing its U

explanation.surface: A setter says a girl enjoys our clues, which are vulgar and not upper-class.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is the British label for speech and habits judged not upper-class; here it just means lose the U's: CLES and S, with LASS inside: C(LASS)LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: An egalitarian society holds all people equal, which is to say it has no social classes.

clue.text: Series of descendants with crown of David ruled

parts.note: a line is a family succession, a lineage

indicators.note: a crown is worn at the top, and the top of a down entry is its first letter

parts.note: the initial letter of David

explanation.surface: The royal descendants of King David, wearing his crown, reigned over Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruled' and 'crown of David' suggest kingship; ruled means marked with straight lines, as paper is.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruled paper has printed straight lines across it, so it is lined paper.

clue.text: Remember, put little old car in salvage (it has no 5th)

indicators.note: put in says to place the car within the salvage word
the salvage word is told it lacks its fifth letter, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: to salvage something is to rescue it
the Mini is the classic small British car

explanation.surface: Recall putting a vintage small car into salvage, minus a fifth gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No 5th' sounds like a car missing its fifth gear; it actually means the salvage word drops its fifth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To reminisce is to talk or think fondly about past events, recalling them.

clue.text: Fabrication by Feds planted in course of seizure

indicators.note: something planted in the course of another thing is set down inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a fit is a sudden seizure or attack
G-men are American federal agents of the FBI

explanation.surface: A story about federal agents planting evidence during a raid and seizure.
explanation.walkthrough: G-men is American slang for FBI agents, short for government men.
explanation.definitionFit: A figment, as in a figment of the imagination, is something invented and untrue, a made-up story.

clue.text: Musical instrument — loud one

parts.note: f is the musical marking forte, loud
one refers back to a musical instrument, here a lute

explanation.surface: A musical instrument that is a loud one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' stands for another instrument, so a lute follows the musical F.
explanation.definitionFit: The flute is a woodwind instrument played by blowing across a hole.

clue.text: Welcome hints of tomato in garlic sprinkled into cabbage

indicators.note: sprinkled into says the letters are scattered at points inside the vegetable word

parts.note: greens are leafy vegetables such as cabbage

indicators.note: hints are just traces, so only the first letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the first letters of tomato, in and garlic

explanation.surface: A recipe: welcome a little tomato in garlic sprinkled over cabbage.
explanation.walkthrough: Sprinkled means the three initials are not inserted as one group: two go together and the third goes in separately, nearer the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Greetings, as an exclamation, is a word of welcome said on meeting someone.

clue.text: Losing head, panic by mistake

indicators.note: losing its head means the word for panic drops its first letter

parts.note: terror is extreme fear, panic

explanation.surface: Someone loses their head and panics by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: TERROR without its T gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, something done wrongly.

clue.text: Fertile layer spilt two eggs — broken

indicators.note: broken eggs fit the surface, and broken letters are reassembled in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
an egg is shaped like O, so two eggs are two O's

explanation.surface: Two eggs were spilt and broke on fertile ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Topsoil is the upper layer of earth where plants grow, rich in organic matter.

clue.text: Commander having office once more

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish military commander or chief
a party in office is said to be in, holding power

explanation.surface: A commander takes up an official post for a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ottoman title for a commander is a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Again is the plain adverb for another time, repeated, once more.

clue.text: Second employment: recurring role in long-running play

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
use is employment, as in putting something to use

indicators.note: recurring is read as running back again, so the word for role is turned round

parts.note: an actor's part is their role

explanation.surface: An actor's second job: a regular role in a show that has run for years.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mousetrap, Agatha Christie's whodunnit, has run in London's West End since 1952.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mousetrap is famously the longest-running stage production in theatre history, so it is the long-running play par excellence.

clue.text: Home team penetrates defence that's not brilliant with run for header

indicators.note: a header is the top of something, so run is placed at the very front

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

indicators.note: to penetrate is to get inside, so the team goes into what is left of the defence
the defence is to lose a word for brilliant, so that slang term is taken away from it

parts.note: taken as written, before the slang word DEF is removed
def is slang, from hip-hop, for excellent or brilliant
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A football report: the home team breaks through a mediocre defence, someone scoring with a header.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Header' and 'team' make it sound like football, but run is the cricket abbreviation, and header just means placed at the top. The team goes in after the first letter of what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A residence is the place where someone lives, their house or dwelling.

clue.text: Top of tree's odd trunk

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, so only the start of tree is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of tree
odd after a number means approximately, as twenty-odd means twenty or so

explanation.surface: The top of a tree is curiously shaped, as is its trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining T + OR SO to the definition. 'Trunk' looks like part of the tree, but it is the human body.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the human trunk, the body without head or limbs.

clue.text: Peas or leeks broadcast round bottom of field are unwanted plants

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the spoken word goes around the selected letter
broadcast means spoken out over the air, so we want words that sound like peas and leeks

parts.note: peas sounds like pees and leeks like leaks, and both are wees, slang for urinating

indicators.note: the bottom of a word written down is its last letter

parts.note: the final letter of field

explanation.surface: Garden vegetables scattered around a field turn out to be unwanted plants.
explanation.walkthrough: Peas and leeks look like the plants; said out loud they are 'pees' and 'leaks', both of which are wees. D goes inside: WEE(D)S.
explanation.definitionFit: Weeds are wild plants growing where they are not wanted, especially among crops.

clue.text: Nasty wound — bike seat needs adjusting round bearing

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the letters go around the bearing
something that needs adjusting is to be reset, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
N, north, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A cyclist with a nasty sore needs the saddle adjusting around a bearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' sounds like a bike part; it is a compass direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A snakebite is the wound left by a snake's fangs, which can be venomous and dangerous.

clue.text: Court charges resulting in bird

parts.note: to spoon is an old word for courting, kissing and cuddling
a bill lists charges to be paid

explanation.surface: Legal proceedings that end up with someone being given a bird, a prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' and 'charges' suggest a trial; court is the verb meaning to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: The spoonbill is a wading bird named for its long, flat bill widened at the tip.

clue.text: For translation go to short old German

indicators.note: a translation turns words into a different form, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tip for translators: go for brevity with old German.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ostrogoths were the eastern Goths, a Germanic people who ruled Italy in the fifth and sixth centuries.

clue.text: I'll go with last of gin, a beer and one tequila for starters in a cocktail

definitions.text: I'll go with last of gin, a beer and one tequila for starters in a cocktail

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so all these letters are mixed together

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the last of a word is its end letter, so only the end of gin is used

parts.note: the final letter of gin
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: starters are what come first, so tequila gives only its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of tequila

explanation.surface: A drinker orders gin, beer and tequila shots all mixed into one cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the drinker and also supplies the letters, so it is both wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An inebriate is a habitual drunkard, exactly the person who would order such a mixture.

clue.text: Will trial endorse Chilcott's conclusion?

parts.note: a test is a trial
to amen something is to say so be it to it, endorsing it

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter, so only the end of Chilcott is used

parts.note: the last letter of Chilcott

explanation.surface: Will a court case back up the findings of the Chilcott inquiry?
explanation.walkthrough: The Chilcott report was the UK's long-awaited official inquiry into the Iraq War, published in 2016.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament is a will, as in the legal phrase last will and testament.

clue.text: Tango with cad and heel (pig!)

parts.note: Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a rotter is a cad, an old-fashioned word for a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A tango partner is a cad and a heel, a real pig.
explanation.walkthrough: Heel and pig look like insults for the cad; the bracket says this heel is a pig's.
explanation.definitionFit: A trotter is a pig's foot, which is eaten as food, so it is literally a pig's heel.

clue.text: Have a doss when Skins is over

indicators.note: something that is over has been turned over, so the word for skins is read backwards

parts.note: peels are the skins of fruit

explanation.surface: Someone has a kip once the TV drama Skins has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: Skins was a British teen drama on TV; here it is fruit skins. Doss is British slang for sleeping rough or having a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a doss, in British slang, is to get some sleep, often somewhere makeshift.

clue.text: Science of jography (sic) studies

indicators.note: of means made up of, so the answer is formed from part of the run of letters that follows

parts.note: the letters run through the end of the first word, the bracketed word and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A misspelling of geography, flagged as such, in a list of school subjects.
explanation.walkthrough: The '(sic)' looks like an editor's note on a misspelling, but its letters are part of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Physics is the science of matter, energy and the forces between them.

clue.text: Fantastic tangle holding you French back

indicators.note: holding means having inside, so the seaweed word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: tangle and ore are both names for a kind of seaweed, oarweed

indicators.note: back says the French word is written backwards

parts.note: tu is the familiar French for you

explanation.surface: A fantastic muddle involving you in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tangle' reads as a muddle, but it is a seaweed, which Chambers also calls ore.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré means eccentric or beyond the bounds of convention, so bizarre or fantastic in the sense of fanciful.

clue.text: Put out lit-up bulb

indicators.note: put out means upset or disturbed, so these letters are thrown into a different order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to switch off a light bulb that is on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' and 'lit-up' suggest a light bulb; it is a flower bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: The tulip grows from a bulb, and gardeners plant tulip bulbs in autumn.

clue.text: Reckless idiot half of double act

parts.note: a fool is an idiot
Oliver Hardy was one half of the comedy double act Laurel and Hardy

explanation.surface: One of a comedy pairing plays the reckless fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurel and Hardy were the classic slapstick duo of early film.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolhardy means bold without thought for the risks, rashly daring.

clue.text: Finally oddly used to stuffiness in composition

indicators.note: finally says this pair of letters is placed at the end

parts.note: a fug is a stuffy, airless atmosphere

indicators.note: oddly picks the letters in odd positions, first and third, of the word used

parts.note: the first and third letters of used

explanation.surface: At last, a curious use of stuffiness in a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: Fug is a British word for warm, stale, smoky air in a room.
explanation.definitionFit: A fugue is a musical composition in which a theme is taken up by successive voices.

clue.text: Theatrical claptrap is certainly in bad odour

indicators.note: in places the word for certainly within the smell word

parts.note: a hum is British slang for a bad smell
OK is an agreeing yes, certainly

explanation.surface: Stage nonsense certainly stinks.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a bad smell is said to hum.
explanation.definitionFit: Hokum is sentimental or melodramatic stage business meant to win applause, and by extension nonsense.

clue.text: 'Royal Highness' is out of line by dressing down

indicators.note: something that is out of a word has been dropped from it, so the letter for line goes

parts.note: read literally, highness is height, so a royal highness is a monarch of great stature
L is the abbreviation for line
by and to both mean near, as in close by and close to

explanation.surface: A royal personage behaves improperly by turning up in casual clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks invite a literal reading: a high king is a TALL KING. Lose one L and add TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A talking-to is a scolding or reprimand, just as a dressing down is a severe telling-off.

clue.text: In Two Thousand And One, its computer is cut off — this is dull material

indicators.note: in sets the shortened name inside the letters from the numbers

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, so two of them give a pair
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: a word cut off loses its end, so the computer's name drops its last letter

parts.note: HAL 9000 is the computer in the film 2001: A Space Odyssey

explanation.surface: In the film 2001, the computer is switched off; a remark about the drab material on show.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invokes 2001: A Space Odyssey, where the computer is disconnected; its shortened name sits between the two thousands, before the one.
explanation.definitionFit: Khaki is a dull brownish-yellow cloth, used for military uniforms.

clue.text: Full theatre's licensed revue at last

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre
to let is to permit or license

indicators.note: at last points to the end of the word, so only its final letter is taken

parts.note: the last letter of revue

explanation.surface: A theatre has finally been granted a licence for its revue.
explanation.definitionFit: Replete means filled or well supplied, especially full after eating.

clue.text: Amateur mercenaries save 100 pounds

parts.note: a ham is an amateur, as in a ham radio operator or ham actor

indicators.note: save here means except, so the hundred is taken away from the mercenaries

parts.note: mercs is the short informal word for hired soldiers
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Inexperienced soldiers of fortune manage to save a hundred quid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pounds' looks like money beside 'save 100'; it is a verb, to beat repeatedly.
explanation.definitionFit: To pound something is to strike it heavily and repeatedly, which is what someone who hammers it does.
